To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

lifestyle migrants are people who move to places where they can live a particular lifestyle that they believe is better for them and their families, and that this lifestyle is based on the idea that they can have more control and balance in their lives.

lifestyle migrants use second homes as transitional or ‘potential spaces’ in the lives to construct a new identity and to reconcile distinct visions of self and the good that underlies a lifestyle commitment to a new place.
the lifestyle migrants we studied use their second homes to negotiate work-family balance and control, and they do so by constructing a potential self.

the role of leisure and lifestyle in migration and with the role of migration in lifestyle.

lifestyle migration is a form of migration that is not only a result of the changing nature of work and family, but also a means by which people attempt to negotiate and balance these changes.
the study of lifestyle migration can help us to understand the ways in which work and family are changing, as well as the ways in which these changes are shaping migration.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how lifestyle migration is an example of how the social construction of identity is an active and ongoing project.
we are interested in the ways that people are using their leisure and leisure places to construct and reconstruct identity and purpose.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the potential self is a key concept in understanding the motivations for and outcomes of lifestyle migration.
lifestyle migration is not simply about ‘escape’ or ‘resistance’ but rather about ‘re-creation’.

the ‘lifestyle commitment’, which we see as a new cultural form, can be understood as the means through which people seek to realise the ‘potential self’, a self that they believe is possible through lifestyle migration and that is not possible within their current lives and circumstances.
